name: 7 Year Bitch
label: C/Z
lede: Four women from Seattle's Capitol Hill lost their guitarist weeks before their first album and named the second for a friend murdered a year later. Atlantic signed them, and in 1997, seven years after they began, they stopped.

eras.title: Fig bars and the Rathouse
eras.text: By Valerie Agnew's account, the band got going while she and Selene Vigil sold fig bars at Pike Place Market. The first show opened for the Gits, and a single was out by 1991.

years.big: "We would just shoot the shit about it while we were selling fig bars."
years.src: There's Something Hard in There · Wikipedia: 7 Year Bitch
years.h: A band starts between customers at Pike Place Market
years.p: Valerie Agnew and Selene Vigil worked at an Italian import shop in the market. Elizabeth Davis was a regular customer, and Stefanie Sargent completed the lineup.
years.xp:
Agnew told the blog There's Something Hard in There that the band began at the shop. Davis, she said, was a customer.

Wikipedia tells it differently: Vigil, Agnew and Sargent were already in Barbie's Dream Car and recruited Davis after their bassist moved to Europe. The name was suggested by their friend Ben London, after the film The Seven Year Itch.

years.src: There's Something Hard in There · Wikipedia: The Gits
years.h: The first show is a support slot for the Gits
years.p: Singer Mia Zapata of [[The Gits|b916a410-ee27-4f15-92ce-1ce2b60e7697]] rehearsed at the Rathouse, and she and Stefanie Sargent became close friends.
years.xp:
Vigil told the same blog that watching Zapata sing was transformative, and described "raw, pure, soul."

The Rathouse was the run-down Capitol Hill house where the Gits lived and practiced, per Wikipedia's Gits article.

years.h: Debut single "Lorna" backed with "No Fucking War"
years.p: It came out on Rathouse and Face the Music, and C/Z Records reissued it in 1992 after signing the band.

eras.title: The record that had to wait
eras.text: C/Z Records signed them and set a July date for the debut. Stefanie Sargent died in June. Sick 'Em came out in October, dedicated to her, with Roisin Dunne on guitar.

years.src: Wikipedia: 7 Year Bitch · Wikipedia: Stefanie Sargent
years.h: Stefanie Sargent dies at 24, weeks before the debut
years.p: Sargent died in her Capitol Hill apartment after eight months of sobriety. Wikipedia says she used alcohol and heroin at a party and died of asphyxiation, and that her bandmates did not know she was struggling.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page gives the date as June 27, 1992; her own article says she was found on June 28. She was known as "Friday."

Westword described it as a heroin overdose during the recording of Sick 'Em. The album was pushed from July to October and dedicated to her.

years.h: Sick 'Em arrives in October, dedicated to Sargent
years.p: Twelve tracks gathering the earlier 7-inches and the Chow Down 10-inch, produced by Scott Benson. Vigil and Davis wrote most of it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the record was made between June 1990 and June 1992, so it reads as a collected first chapter more than one session. Trouser Press called it "a fairly primitive and monochromatic burst of punk rage."

Agnew later said ¡Viva Zapata! improved on its murky production.

years.h: Roisin Dunne picks up Sargent's guitar
years.p: Dunne joined in the months after Sargent's death and stayed until August 1996, through the Atlantic deal.

eras.title: The Zapata year
eras.text: Mia Zapata of the Gits was murdered in July 1993. The band's best-known record carried her name, and Agnew helped start Home Alive.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Gits · Wikipedia: Valerie Agnew · Denver Westword
years.h: Mia Zapata is murdered walking home from the Comet Tavern
years.p: The Gits' singer, a close friend of the band, was raped and murdered in Seattle. Two days later 7 Year Bitch played the Mural Amphitheater, and the case stayed unsolved for nearly ten years.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's Gits article says DNA evidence identified Jesus Mezquia in December 2002. He was arrested in Miami in January 2003 and convicted in March 2004, receiving a 36-year sentence.

Agnew had dated Gits drummer Steve Moriarty before moving to Seattle and was close to Zapata, per her Wikipedia page. She told Westword: "There have been seven deaths in the last two years that affected us directly."

years.h: Valerie Agnew helps found Home Alive
years.p: She and eight other women started the Seattle self-defense group after Zapata's murder, with classes on a sliding scale.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits nine co-founders and says Home Alive closed as a nonprofit in 2010 after 17 years. Its 1995 compilation Home Alive: The Art of Self Defense had 44 tracks by Seattle artists.

years.h: A Miami benefit, the day Kurt Cobain's death is announced
years.p: 7 Year Bitch played the Cameo Theatre with Babes in Toyland and Jack Off Jill at a Rock Against Domestic Violence show.

q: It's a tribute. And it's a very personal thing.
years.h: Jack Endino records ¡Viva Zapata! at Avast!
years.p: The title and cover honor Zapata, and the band dedicated the record to Sargent too. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 34 on a 2019 list of the 50 greatest grunge albums.
years.xp:
Davis called it "a tribute" and "a very personal thing." Vigil told Westword that grief was not an intended theme: "There's not really a theme."

Entertainment Weekly called the band's take on feminism "rather revolutionary."

years.h: They cover the Jim Carroll Band's "It's Too Late"
years.p: Track 7 of ¡Viva Zapata! is the band's version of the Jim Carroll Band song.

years.h: Duncan Sharp directs the "Hip Like Junk" video
years.p: Filmed in Seattle that August, for a track off ¡Viva Zapata!.

eras.title: The Atlantic years
eras.text: A major-label deal, two songs in a Drew Barrymore movie, and a heavier album made with a producer Neurosis recommended. Then the guitarist left and a European tour was cancelled.

years.cap: Selene Vigil at Pain in the Grass, Seattle Center, August 1995
yt: Pain in the Grass, Seattle, Aug. 18, 1995
years.h: Atlantic signs them, and Drew Barrymore's Mad Love uses two songs
years.p: "The Scratch" and "Icy Blue" from ¡Viva Zapata! play in the film, which stars Barrymore and Chris O'Donnell.

years.h: Neurosis recommends the producer for Gato Negro
years.p: The band recorded it over three weeks in October 1995 at Brilliant Studios in San Francisco with Billy Anderson, for Atlantic. It's heavier and slower than ¡Viva Zapata!.
years.xp:
Davis wrote the music and Vigil the lyrics and vocal lines. Agnew said the band feared sounding "really slick or pumped up."

Reviews split: Entertainment Weekly called it "a humorless clutch of tough-grrrl conventions," while others praised the growth.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gato Negro · Wikipedia: 7 Year Bitch
years.h: Sound engineer Lisa Fay Beatty takes over guitar
years.p: Roisin Dunne leaves in August and a European tour is cancelled. Beatty, the band's live sound engineer and a longtime friend, steps in after a spring headline tour and the Summerland Tour with Everclear.

eras.title: Seven years, then done
eras.text: Davis and Agnew moved to San Francisco, Vigil to Los Angeles. The band toured one last time with Lost Goat and ended.

years.cap: Elizabeth Davis on bass at Pain in the Grass, Seattle Center, August 1995
years.h: 7 Year Bitch ends on tour with Lost Goat
years.p: With the members now split between San Francisco and Los Angeles, the band played a final run and split, seven years after it began.

eras.title: Benefit shows and a lost tape
eras.text: Members went on to Clone, Von Iva and solo records. In 2015 the band played one benefit, and in 2016 a 1996 club tape came out.

years.cap: The band on a panel at MoPOP, Seattle, January 2016
years.h: Back on stage at Chop Suey for Hammerbox's James Atkins
years.p: The benefit raised money for Atkins, who was fighting esophageal cancer. The Gits reunited too, with Visqueen's Rachel Flotard singing.
years.xp: Vigil told Do206 it was "one of the best experiences of my life." Alcohol Funnycar and Hammerbox also played, per The Stranger.

years.cap: The band laughing on the MoPOP panel, Seattle, January 17, 2016
years.h: A 1996 Club Moe tape turns up in a basement
years.p: Producer Scott Blum found the recording at home, and Moe Recordings put out Live at Moe in January.
years.xp: The set was recorded at Seattle's Club Moe in 1996. Vigil told Do206 hearing it was "a full body experience, chills, tears, smiles, nail biting, joy, heartache."
